identity.title: Global Resolution: Optimal Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Convex Optimization

problem.claim: Efficiently compute the acceptance-maximizing verification criterion for multi-draft speculative sampling.

gap.claim: Existing formulations remain infeasible because they correspond to exponentially large optimization problems.

contributions.claim: Reformulates the optimal multi-draft transport problem as a max-flow problem and then reduces it to convex optimization with at most V variables using polymatroid theory.
Provides an algorithm for optimal n-draft speculative sampling when draft tokens are sampled i.i.d. from one draft model, tunable to arbitrary accuracy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their polymatroid-theoretic reduction as novel and their result as the first multi-draft algorithm reporting 90% acceptance with under 100 ms overhead per generated token and negligible target-distribution deviation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report measuring acceptance rates and algorithm runtimes across various n and top-k draft-sampling settings.
The authors report 90% acceptance, under 100 ms overhead per generated token, and negligible deviation from the target model distribution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Speculative sampling uses a cheap draft model and verification to reduce autoregressive decoding latency without sacrificing inference quality, as described by the authors.
Multi-draft sampling generates n draft tokens per step, with verification conditioned on them; the acceptance-maximizing criterion is called optimal transport.
The direct optimal-transport linear program is difficult because it has V^n variables, and prior reformulations remain exponentially large.
The authors reverse-engineer subset selection into max-flow and apply polymatroid theory to obtain a convex problem with at most V variables and an arbitrarily accurate algorithm.
They measure acceptance and runtime under varied draft counts and top-k settings, reporting high acceptance and low overhead with negligible distribution deviation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects an infeasible exponential formulation to a max-flow formulation and then to a convex problem with at most V variables.

lessons.interpretation: A strong algorithmic narrative can make each reformulation serve as an explicit bridge from computational obstacle to tractable implementation.
lessons.application: When presenting a new optimization method, state the size of the original problem, identify the intermediate structural reformulation, and quantify the final reduction in dimensionality.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the main contribution is empirical, conceptual, or not based on successive equivalent reformulations.

unknowns: The abstract does not quantify “arbitrary accuracy,” “negligible deviation,” or the exact acceptance/runtime measurement protocol.
The reported 90% acceptance and under-100-ms overhead are not tied to specific n, vocabulary size, hardware, or top-k settings.
The abstract does not provide baselines or detailed comparisons against prior algorithms.
